correctness.rationale: Proved exact normal geometry; all 64 sign masks and 30 directed intersections checked in Q(sqrt5) with a finite exhaustive chamber-vertex theorem. The 32 distinct cells have verified 10/20/2 shadow counts, exact physical spherical-angle multisets and Girard area formulas. Independent direct hull reconstructions agree for 10000 random orientations; numerical checks supplement the finite exhaustive proof.

evidence: Glisse–Lazard 2007 proves an average bound in terms of size and surface approximation rather than exact distribution for the ten-vertex uniform antiprism.
Glisse et al. 2016 randomize polytopes sampled on a sphere and study maximal silhouette complexity; their theorems are not fixed-solid Haar PMFs.
The general antiprism expectation fixes E[N]=6.722110996233718 but permits infinitely many distinct 6/8/10 PMFs with that mean.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These broader average-complexity and dihedral-angle results do not imply all three atom probabilities or the exact 32-region chamber classification. A generic algorithm for computing silhouettes is not itself the resulting exact law.

originality.rationale: Compared actual implication with published 2007 average-bound and 2016 random-polytope sources, a published central regular-icosahedron section law, available full antiprism mean theorem and explicit database searches. None of accessible scientific statements implies the exact fixed uniform pentagonal antiprism 6/8/10 PMF. Full 1997 predecessor unavailable, retained priority risk. residual_risks: Kettner–Welzl 1997 full article remains inaccessible due to institutional-connection requirement; an exact earlier antiprism case cannot be categorically excluded.

value.rationale: Uniform pentagonal antiprism is a canonical Archimedean family member. Complete and exact all-orientation silhouette PMF and full 32-chamber stratification go substantively beyond the known mean. The rare 10-vertex probability distinguishes tail geometry useful in rendering/geometry, and the finite normal-arrangement method extends naturally to other polyhedra; object and statistic are non-arbitrary.
